blogs.title: When DIC Isn’t the Whole Story: Spotting TMA After Sepsis Begins to Improve
blogs.description: This post would examine the diagnostic pivot point in this case: a patient with clear septic DIC who later developed persistent thrombocytopenia, worsening kidney injury, schistocytosis and overt haemolysis despite improving infection markers. It would focus on how thrombotic microangiopathy can be masked early by sepsis-related coagulopathy, and how clinicians can recognize the transition from 'expected critical illness labs' to a second superimposed process requiring a different treatment pathway.

blogs.title: Dog Bite, Pancytopenia, Shock: Why Capnocytophaga Belongs on the Early Differential
blogs.description: This post would review the emergency and ICU implications of Capnocytophaga canimorsus infection after dog exposure, especially in patients who do not fit the classic immunocompromised profile. It would cover the organism’s fastidious nature, delayed culture confirmation, severe presentations including DIC and multiorgan failure, and practical empiric antibiotic considerations after dog bites when a patient looks much sicker than the wound suggests.

blogs.title: MAHA in the ICU: TTP, STEC-HUS, CM-HUS, or Something Else?
blogs.description: This post would use the case to build a pragmatic diagnostic framework for adult thrombotic microangiopathy. It would discuss how to approach MAHA, thrombocytopenia and AKI in real time, including the role and limitations of PLASMIC scoring, ADAMTS13 activity, stool Shiga toxin testing, peripheral smear review, DAT interpretation, and kidney biopsy. The emphasis would be on separating TTP from complement-mediated HUS quickly enough to guide therapy.

blogs.title: Normal C3, Normal C4, Still aHUS: The Complement Testing Trap
blogs.description: This post would tackle one of the most important teaching points in the case: normal routine complement studies do not exclude complement-mediated HUS. It would explain why CM-HUS remains a clinical diagnosis of exclusion, how timing of plasma exchange and eculizumab can distort extended complement assays, and why clinicians should avoid over-relying on standard C3/C4 results when the clinical picture strongly suggests complement-mediated TMA.

blogs.title: Eculizumab During or After Infection? Managing Complement Blockade in Infection-Triggered HUS
blogs.description: This post would explore the management tension at the heart of the case: complement blockade is the definitive therapy for CM-HUS, yet terminal complement is also crucial for host defense against encapsulated organisms. It would discuss when to start plasma exchange as bridging therapy, how clinicians balance ongoing infection risk against the harm of delaying eculizumab, and the logistics of meningococcal vaccination, antibiotic prophylaxis and monitoring when urgent complement inhibition cannot wait.

blogs.title: From Anuria to Partial Recovery: What Renal Biopsy and Clinical Course Teach Us About Prognosis in CM-HUS
blogs.description: This post would focus on the nephrology lessons from the case, including the significance of complete anuria, dialysis dependence, and biopsy findings showing acute tubular necrosis plus glomerular fibrin thrombi. It would review what predicts renal recovery in complement-mediated HUS, how late recognition may limit kidney outcomes even when haematologic remission is achieved, and how to think about duration of eculizumab therapy when genetic testing is negative but the initial kidney injury was severe.
